scheme_name: Vadh Se Bachaye Govansh Ko Sahayata Yojana
description:
The Vadh Se Bachaye Govansh Ko Sahayata Yojana is a welfare scheme launched by the Government of India to provide assistance to farmers and livestock owners in protecting their cattle from the adverse effects of climate change and natural disasters.

This scheme was officially launched on 1st July 2021 by the Ministry of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

The primary objective of the Vadh Se Bachaye Govansh Ko Sahayata Yojana is to ensure the safety and welfare of cattle during extreme weather conditions such as floods and droughts.

The scheme aims to reduce the mortality rate of livestock by providing financial assistance to farmers for the treatment and care of their animals.

The measurable target set by the government is to reduce livestock mortality by at least 30 percent in the regions most affected by climate change.

The scheme also aims to promote awareness among farmers regarding the importance of livestock health and management practices.

Under this scheme, farmers can receive financial assistance of up to INR 30,000 per animal for treatment and care.

This financial support is intended to cover veterinary expenses, feed costs, and other necessary expenditures related to livestock care.

Eligibility for the Vadh Se Bachaye Govansh Ko Sahayata Yojana is primarily focused on small and marginal farmers.

Farmers must own at least one bovine animal to qualify for the assistance.

The income limit for eligibility is set at INR 2 lakh per annum for the family.

Farmers must also provide proof of ownership of the livestock they seek assistance for.

The application process for the scheme involves several steps to ensure transparency and accountability.

Farmers must first visit the official website of the Ministry of Animal Husbandry and Dairying to download the application form.

The completed application form must be submitted to the local veterinary office along with required documents.

Required documents include proof of identity such as an Aadhar card, proof of ownership of the animal, and income certificate.

Once the application is submitted, it will be verified by the local veterinary officer.

The verification process typically takes about 15 to 30 days.

After successful verification, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account.

The timeline for application submission is open throughout the year.

However, farmers are encouraged to apply as soon as they face adverse conditions affecting their livestock.

Disbursement of funds is usually processed within 15 days after verification.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Animal Husbandry and Dairying at the central level.

At the state level, the respective Animal Husbandry Departments are responsible for the execution of the scheme.

Farmers can contact the local veterinary office for any queries related to the scheme.

The contact details of the Ministry of Animal Husbandry and Dairying can be found on their official website.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of community participation in livestock management.

Workshops and training sessions are organized to educate farmers about best practices in animal husbandry.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crore for the implementation of this scheme in the initial phase.

This budget is aimed at covering the costs of treatment and care for approximately 1.67 million bovine animals.

The scheme is particularly beneficial for farmers in regions prone to natural disasters such as floods and droughts.

In the first year of implementation, the government reported a significant increase in the number of applications received.

Over 200,000 farmers applied for assistance in the first six months of the scheme's launch.

The government aims to expand the reach of the scheme to cover more farmers in the coming years.

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted regularly to assess its impact on livestock health.

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme's effectiveness and reach.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the government to enhance the livelihoods of farmers and promote sustainable agriculture.

The Vadh Se Bachaye Govansh Ko Sahayata Yojana is aligned with the National Livestock Policy which aims to improve livestock productivity and welfare.

The government also collaborates with various NGOs and organizations to promote awareness about the scheme.

Farmers are encouraged to participate in community health camps organized under this scheme.

These camps provide free veterinary services and health check-ups for livestock.

The scheme is expected to contribute to the overall economic stability of rural areas by ensuring livestock health.

By protecting livestock, the scheme also aims to secure the income of farmers who rely on animal husbandry for their livelihoods.

The government has also initiated a digital platform to streamline the application process for farmers.

This platform allows farmers to track their application status and receive updates on disbursement.

The Vadh Se Bachaye Govansh Ko Sahayata Yojana is an important step towards building resilience in the agricultural sector.

It addresses the challenges posed by climate change and aims to safeguard the livelihoods of millions of farmers across India.

The scheme is designed to be inclusive and accessible to all eligible farmers.

The government is committed to ensuring that no farmer is left behind in accessing the benefits of this scheme.

Overall, the Vadh Se Bachaye Govansh Ko Sahayata Yojana represents a proactive approach to livestock management in India.

It reflects the government's dedication to improving the welfare of farmers and their animals in the face of environmental challenges.
